title: "Reference"

## All Options

All project and document options are set under `extensions: term:` — in `_quarto.yml` for project-wide defaults, or in a document's front matter to override per file. Cell options use `#|` at the top of a cell. Line options use the marker (default `#!`) at the end of a line.

### General Options

| Option | Project | Document | Cell | Line | Default | Description |
|--------|:-------:|:--------:|:----:|:----:|---------|-------------|
| `callouts` | | | x | | `[]` | Line indices or patterns to annotate with callout markers |
| `delay` | | | x | x | `0.1` | Seconds to wait before executing a line |
| `echo` | | | x | | `terminal` | Output mode: `terminal`, `source`, `true`, or `false` |
| `enter` | | | | x | (from `literal`) | Press Enter after the line |
| `env` | x | x | | | `{}` | Additional environment variables |
| `eval` | | | x | | `true` | Execute the cell; `false` renders it as a static code block |
| `expect-prompt` | | | | x | (from `enter`) | Wait for prompt after the line |
| `fullscreen` | | | x | | `false` | Capture the entire terminal screen |
| `highlight` | | | x | | `bash` | Syntax highlighting language (for `echo: source`) |
| `hold` | | | x | x | `0.1` (line) | Seconds to wait after execution (captures ongoing output) |
| `include` | | | x | | `true` | Execute the cell but hide it entirely from output |
| `init` | x | x | | | (none) | Script(s) or command(s) to run at session start |
| `keep-last-prompt` | | | x | | `false` | Keep the trailing prompt in output |
| `label` | | | x | | (none) | Cell label (shown in verbose mode) |
| `literal` | | | x | x | `true` | Send text as typed characters; `false` for key names |
| `marker` | x | x | x | | `#!` | Prefix for line option annotations |
| `output` | | | x | | `true` | Show terminal output |
| `prompt` | x | x | | | `$` | Literal prompt string (auto-sets `PS1`) |
| `prompt-regex` | x | x | | | (derived) | Raw regex override for prompt detection |
| `record` | x | x | | | (none) | File path(s) to record session (`.cast` or `.termshow`) |
| `remove` | | | x | | `[]` | Line indices or patterns to remove from output |
| `scroll` | | | x | | `!fullscreen` | Include scrollback in capture |
| `shell` | x | x | | | `zsh` | Shell to use |
| `shell-args` | x | x | | | (auto) | Shell arguments |
| `spacing` | x | x | x | | `false` | Add blank lines between commands in output |
| `timeout` | x | x | x | | `10.0` | Seconds to wait for prompt before error |
| `typing` | x | x | x | | `false` | Human typing simulation |
| `verbose` | x | x | | | `false` | Print execution details to stderr |

### Style Options

Style options live under `style:` and control the visual appearance of terminal output. They support format-specific overrides (see below).

| Option | Project | Document | Cell | Default | Description |
|--------|:-------:|:--------:|:----:|---------|-------------|
| `colorscheme` | x | x | x | (none) | Color theme name |
| `colorscheme-light` | x | x | x | (none) | Theme for light mode |
| `colorscheme-dark` | x | x | x | (none) | Theme for dark mode |
| `font-family` | x | x | x | (none) | Font family for terminal output |
| `font-size` | x | x | x | (none) | Font size (e.g., `0.85em`) |
| `line-height` | x | x | x | (none) | Line height (e.g., `1.2`) |
| `ansi` | x | x | x | `true` | Render ANSI colors in output |
| `trailing-spaces` | x | x | x | `false` | Preserve trailing whitespace in output |
| `cols` | x | x | | `80` | Terminal width in columns |
| `rows` | x | x | | `24` | Terminal height in rows |

### Format-Specific Overrides

Style options can be overridden per output format by nesting them under a format key within `style:`:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    style:
      colorscheme: dracula
      font-size: 0.9em
      cols: 80
      html:
        colorscheme-light: github-light
        colorscheme-dark: github-dark
      pdf:
        cols: 60
        font-size: 0.75em
      revealjs:
        cols: 64
        font-size: 0.65em
```

Recognized format keys: `html`, `pdf`, `revealjs`, `typst`, `epub`, `markdown`, `latex`.

### Per-Cell Style

Override style for individual cells using dotted keys or a nested block. The full style functionality is available at the cell level, including format-specific overrides.

Dotted keys:

````markdown
```{term}
#| style.colorscheme: nord
#| style.font-size: 0.8em
echo "Styled cell"
```
````

Nested block:

````markdown
```{term}
#| style:
#|   colorscheme: nord
#|   font-size: 0.8em
echo "Styled cell"
```
````

Format-specific overrides at the cell level:

````markdown
```{term}
#| style.font-size: 0.9em
#| style.html.font-size: 0.8em
#| style.revealjs.font-size: 0.65em
echo "Different sizes per format"
```
````

Or with a nested block:

````markdown
```{term}
#| style:
#|   colorscheme: dracula
#|   html:
#|     colorscheme-light: github-light
#|     colorscheme-dark: github-dark
#|   revealjs:
#|     font-size: 0.65em
echo "Format-aware cell"
```
````

Per-cell style options: `colorscheme`, `colorscheme-light`, `colorscheme-dark`, `font-family`, `font-size`, `line-height`, `ansi`, `trailing-spaces`. Note that `cols` and `rows` cannot be set per-cell because the PTY is shared across all cells in a session.

## Document-Level Options

Set these under `extensions: term:` in your YAML front matter:

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `shell` | `zsh` | Shell to use |
| `shell-args` | auto | Shell arguments (defaults: `--no-rcs` for zsh, `--norc --noprofile` for bash) |
| `prompt` | `$` | Literal prompt string. Auto-sets `PS1` and builds the matching regex. |
| `prompt-regex` | (derived) | Raw regex override for prompt detection |
| `timeout` | `10.0` | Seconds to wait for prompt before error |
| `spacing` | `false` | Add blank lines between commands in output |
| `marker` | `#!` | Prefix for line option annotations |
| `typing` | `false` | Human typing simulation (see below) |
| `record` | (none) | File path to record session (`.cast` or `.termshow`) |
| `verbose` | `false` | Print execution details to stderr |
| `init` | (none) | Script(s) or command(s) to run at session start (string or list) |
| `env` | `{}` | Additional environment variables |
| `style` | (none) | Style options (see above) |

## Cell Options

Set these with `#|` at the top of a cell:

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `eval` | `true` | Execute the cell; `false` renders it as a static code block |
| `include` | `true` | Execute the cell but hide it entirely from output |
| `label` | (none) | Cell label (shown in verbose mode) |
| `echo` | `terminal` | Output mode: `terminal`, `source`, `true`, or `false` |
| `output` | `true` | Show terminal output |
| `fullscreen` | `false` | Capture the entire terminal screen |
| `scroll` | `!fullscreen` | Include scrollback in capture |
| `keep-last-prompt` | `false` | Keep the trailing prompt in output |
| `spacing` | (from config) | Override spacing for this cell |
| `typing` | (from config) | Override typing simulation |
| `timeout` | (from config) | Override timeout for this cell |
| `hold` | (none) | Seconds to wait after cell completes (captures ongoing output) |
| `literal` | `true` | Default `literal` for all lines in this cell |
| `delay` | `0.1` | Default `delay` for all lines in this cell |
| `highlight` | `bash` | Syntax highlighting language (for `echo: source`) |
| `marker` | (from config) | Override line marker for this cell |
| `style` | (from config) | Override style options for this cell, including format-specific overrides (see [Per-Cell Style](#per-cell-style)) |

## Line Options

Traditional code engines just *execute* code; they send an entire block to an interpreter and capture whatever comes back. quarto-term is different: it *simulates a human typing at a terminal*. Each line is sent to the shell individually, keystroke by keystroke, just as you would type it yourself.

This distinction matters because a real terminal session has *timing*. You might type a command, wait for output to settle, then send a keystroke to interact with what's on screen. You can't express that in a flat code block, but you can with line options.

Line options give you control over *how* each line is delivered to the shell: whether it's typed as literal characters or interpreted as a key name, whether Enter is pressed, how long to pause before or after, and whether to wait for the prompt to return. This is what makes it possible to drive interactive applications, interrupt long-running commands, and produce recordings with natural pacing.

Append options to any line using the marker (default `#!`):

````markdown
```{term}
sleep 100 #! expect-prompt: false
ctrl-c #! literal: false, delay: 0.5, expect-prompt: true
```
````

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `literal` | `true` | Send text as typed characters. Set to `false` for key names. |
| `enter` | (from literal) | Press Enter after the line |
| `expect-prompt` | (from enter) | Wait for prompt after the line |
| `delay` | `0.1` | Seconds to wait *before* executing this line |
| `hold` | `0.1` | Seconds to wait after executing (captures output) |

### Multiple Keys Per Line

When `literal: false`, you can put multiple space-separated key names on a single line. Each key is sent individually, with the line's `delay` value as a pause between them:

````markdown
```{term}
echo "hello"
up enter #! literal: false, delay: 0.2
```
````

This sends the `up` key, waits 0.2 seconds, then sends `enter`. Only the last key on the line triggers `hold` and `expect-prompt`.

To avoid repeating `#! literal: false` on every line, set it as a cell default:

````markdown
```{term}
#| literal: false
#| delay: 0.2
up
enter
```
````

Individual lines can still override the cell default with explicit line options.

## Special Keys

When `literal: false`, these key names are recognized:

- `enter` (also `return`, `cr`), `tab`, `space`
- `escape` (also `esc`), `backspace` (also `bs`), `delete` (also `del`)
- `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `home`, `end`
- `page-up` (also `pageup`), `page-down` (also `pagedown`), `insert`
- `f1` through `f12`

Any other text is sent as raw bytes (e.g., `q` sends the letter q without pressing Enter).

### Modifier Combinations

All modifier prefixes can be combined freely in any order:

| Prefix | Shorthand | Example |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| `ctrl-` | `c-` | `ctrl-c`, `c-c` |
| `shift-` | `s-` | `shift-a`, `s-a` |
| `alt-` | `m-`, `meta-` | `alt-a`, `m-a` |

Combinations are supported: `ctrl-shift-a`, `ctrl-alt-a`, `alt-shift-up`, `ctrl-alt-shift-a`.

Modifiers work with single characters and with special keys:

- `shift-a` sends uppercase `A`
- `ctrl-c` sends the control character (0x03)
- `alt-f` sends the CSI u sequence for Alt+f
- `ctrl-shift-up` sends the modified arrow sequence
- `shift-f5` sends the modified function key sequence

## Human Typing Simulation

Simulate realistic human typing for recordings:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    typing:
      mode: human
      speed: 100        # characters per minute
      error-rate: 0.02  # probability of a typo per character
```

When a "typo" occurs, the simulated typist hits a QWERTY-adjacent key and then corrects with backspace. Timing follows a log-normal distribution with bigram-aware adjustments.

Disable typing for individual cells with `#| typing: false`.

## Prompt Detection

By default, quarto-term uses the literal `prompt` value (default `$`) to detect when a command has finished. It:

1. Sets `PS1` to `prompt + " "` (e.g., `$ `) in the shell environment.
2. Builds a regex from `regex::escape(prompt) + "\\s*$"` to match the prompt in output.

For advanced use cases, override the regex directly:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    prompt: "myhost>"
    prompt-regex: "(\\$|#|myhost>)\\s*$"
```

PS2 (continuation prompt) is auto-set to `"> "` for multi-line command detection.

## Init Scripts

Run commands or source scripts at session start using `init`. Each entry can be a plugin name, a file path, or an inline command:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    init:
      - zsh-syntax-highlighting
      - "setopt INTERACTIVE_COMMENTS"
```

For plugin names, quarto-term checks the current working directory, then searches common installation paths:

- `./<name>` (current working directory)
- `/opt/homebrew/share/<name>/<name>.zsh` (macOS Homebrew)
- `/usr/local/share/<name>/<name>.zsh` (manual installs)
- `/usr/share/<name>/<name>.zsh` (Linux packages)
- `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/share/<name>/<name>.zsh` (Linuxbrew)

Entries that resolve to a file are sourced; everything else is executed as an inline command. Multi-line blocks are split and run line by line:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    init:
      - zsh-syntax-highlighting
      - |
        setopt INTERACTIVE_COMMENTS
        alias ll="ls -la"
        export EDITOR=vim
```

You can also pass an absolute path directly:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    init: "/path/to/my-plugin.zsh"
```

## Terminal Recordings

Record your session for playback:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    record: "session.cast"
```

Supported formats (detected by file extension):

- `.cast` - asciicast v2 format, playable with [asciinema](https://asciinema.org/)
- `.termshow` - termshow format (auto-generates a companion `.termshow.yml`), works with the [termshow](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-docs/) player

You can record to multiple files simultaneously. This is useful for producing both formats in a single render:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    record:
      - "session.cast"
      - "session.termshow"
```

| `catppuccin-frappe` | Medium dark with pastel accents |

### Light Themes

| Theme | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `ayu-light` | Crisp white with warm accents |
| `catppuccin-latte` | Cream-colored with pastels |
| `everforest-light` | Warm paper with nature greens |

| `rose-pine-dawn` | Warm rose-tinged light theme |
| `solarized-light` | Precision-engineered light palette |

Single colorscheme:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    style:
      colorscheme: solarized-dark
```

### Light/Dark Mode

For documents that support Quarto's light/dark toggle, provide both:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme:
      light: flatly
      dark: darkly
extensions:
  term:
    style:
      colorscheme-light: solarized-light
      colorscheme-dark: solarized-dark
```

The terminal blocks automatically switch themes when the user toggles the page between light and dark mode.

## Output Formats

quarto-term produces styled terminal output for all major Quarto output formats.

| Format | Style support | Notes |
|--------|--------------|-------|
| HTML | Full | All style options, ANSI colors as styled spans |
| RevealJS | Full | Same as HTML with CSS specificity overrides |
| PDF (LaTeX) | Full | tcolorbox with colored text, fontspec for fonts |
| PDF (Typst) | Full | Styled block with colored text runs |
| Word (docx) | Full | OpenXML table with styled monospace runs |
| PowerPoint (pptx) | Full | Same renderer as docx |
| EPUB | Full | Same as HTML (EPUB uses XHTML) |
| Markdown/GFM | Text only | Plain text in fenced code blocks (no styling) |
| ODT | Full | Same renderer as docx |

Use format-specific style overrides to optimize the terminal appearance for each output:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    style:
      colorscheme: dracula
      font-size: 0.9em
      pdf:
        font-size: 0.75em
        cols: 60
      typst:
        font-family: "Fira Code"
        font-size: 9pt
      docx:
        font-family: "Consolas"
        font-size: 10pt
      revealjs:
        cols: 64
        font-size: 0.65em
```
